summary: Okta SCIM email normalization strips alias domain leading to CLI/service-account RBAC mismatch
description: Issue summary: After a recent SCIM attribute normalization change in the Okta -> SCIM push flow, some service accounts and developer CLI tokens are failing to receive expected RBAC roles. Impact: ~12 engineers and 3 CI service accounts in prod-us-west report 403s when calling internal APIs; automated deploys using CLI tokens are failing to authenticate with 'role not assigned' errors. This appears correlated with Okta pushing 'email' values that had alias domains (user+alias@example.com) being normalized to 'user@example.com' by the SCIM provisioner, while RBAC mappings still expect the original alias string. Environment: production (us-west), identity-service v2.14.2, scim-provisioner container image sha: a1b2c3d. Steps to reproduce and observed outputs are below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create Okta user with primary email 'eng+ci@example.com' and assign internal 'dev-tools' group.
2) Trigger SCIM push (manual or scheduled sync) to identity-service.
3) Inspect user record in identity-service /users endpoint and RBAC bindings for the account.
4) Attempt CLI login with 'eng+ci@example.com' service token or use associated service-account token in CI and call internal API requiring 'dev-tools' role.

Expected: user has 'dev-tools' role and API call succeeds. Observed: user record in identity-service shows normalized 'eng@example.com' in the 'email' field but SCIM group mapping stored the role under 'eng+ci@example.com' key, resulting in no role match and 403 from RBAC engine.
observed_behavior: SCIM push normalizes alias-style emails (strip '+TAG') before storing on the canonical email field, but group-to-principal mapping keys retain the original alias form. Result: mismatch between principal identifier used for RBAC lookups and the canonical user record. Failing calls return 403 with error code RBAC_MISSING_ROLE and logs show "principal lookup failed: key mismatch".
expected_behavior: Canonicalization should be consistent: either normalize both the principal keys and stored emails to the same form, or preserve the original alias on both sides so RBAC mapping succeeds. No user or CI account should lose roles after a SCIM sync.
logs: identity-service[2026-03-11T08:12:23Z] ERROR rbactree.go:214 principal lookup failed: key mismatch (queried 'eng+ci@example.com', stored 'eng@example.com')
scim-provisioner[2026-03-11T08:12:20Z] INFO sync.go:98 applied user update: id=U-556, email=eng@example.com (normalized from eng+ci@example.com)
cli-auth[2026-03-11T08:13:02Z] WARN token_validator.go:47 authorization denied: RBAC_MISSING_ROLE
comments: 2026-03-11 09:02 - Jocelyn Park: Initial report from developer Slack (#internal-support). Noticed after last week's identity migration. Assigning to auth team for triage.

2026-03-11 10:30 - Ravi Patel: I can reproduce locally against prod-us-west snapshot. The SCIM handler calls NormalizeEmail() downstream; RBAC insertion uses original Okta.Username. Investigating where canonicalization split occurs.

2026-03-11 14:15 - SRE (Maya Singh): CI deploys impacted: build-220/infra and build-221/analytics. Temporarily disabled automated deploys that use eng+ci@example.com tokens to prevent repeated failures.

2026-03-12 08:40 - Ravi Patel: Narrowed root cause to identity-service PR #1892 (email normalization) merged to main and rolled in image a1b2c3d. Creating a patch to align RBAC principal keying with normalized email. Will push hotfix to staging for validation.
2026-03-12 12:02 - Jocelyn Park: Customer-facing teams notified affected engineers through #internal-support; ticket created to track follow-ups and audit items.
investigation_notes: Normalization routine: NormalizeEmail() strips any +alias components (RFC local-part plus tagging) and lowercases domain. Applied during user update path but not applied to GroupPrincipal keys when group membership is created via SCIM 'addMember' calls.
Historical behavior: prior to v2.14.2 both code paths used raw Okta.Username; a refactor introduced normalization on user writes but missed group-key path.

Scope: ~15 user principals affected in prod-us-west (mix of human dev users and CI service accounts). No evidence of lost data beyond RBAC mismatch; audit logs show membership present but under differing principal key forms.

Hypothesis: A two-step remediation can work: 1) Backfill RBAC bindings to use normalized keys for existing memberships. 2) Patch scim-provisioner to normalize principal keys on future membership events.
resolution: Workaround applied: SRE backfilled RBAC bindings for the 15 affected principals to use normalized emails; CI automated deploys temporarily switched to hashed service tokens that bypass principal lookups. Hotfix branch created (PR 1901) — staged patch includes applying NormalizeEmail() for group principal keys and a migration task to reconcile existing bindings. Plan: Run migration during maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00-03:00 UTC, then roll patch to prod-us-west. Post-mortem and audit entries will be created after rollback window.
